title: Putin Links Kerala Teen's AI Work to Modi's 'Make in India' at Moscow Conference
excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin told 16-year-old Raul John Aju that his AI tools help young people find their own solutions, after the Kochi student argued students should master the basics before leaning on AI.
body:
• Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' vision during an exchange with 16-year-old Indian AI innovator Raul John Aju in Moscow on November 26.
  • Putin had asked the Kochi student whether growing use of AI threatens education; Aju argued students should master the basics first, then use AI as a tool.
  • Aju is a Class 12 commerce student who founded AI Realm Technologies and has built a string of AI tools while still in school.
  • The interaction closed the plenary session of the AI Journey 2026 conference, which runs November 26-28 and has drawn more than 300 specialists.

Russian President Vladimir Putin used an interaction with a 16-year-old Indian student in Moscow to praise Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' vision, telling the teenager that his work helps young people develop their own solutions and put them into action. The exchange took place on November 26 at the end of the plenary session of the 'Journey to the World of Artificial Intelligence' conference, according to IANS.

Putin asked Raul John Aju whether the growing use of artificial intelligence poses a threat to the education process. Aju replied that students should work alongside AI rather than depend on it entirely. Drawing a comparison with calculators, he said students should first build a sound understanding of basic concepts before using technology to enhance their learning.

"Artificial intelligence at some stage can be connected to the education process when you are already quite educated, you understand the basics, you understand how you can learn, how to remember."

— Raul John Aju, speaking at AI Journey 2026

Aju added that AI can help students look for new ideas and collect data, but cautioned that the technology is not always a blessing and must be used responsibly. Responding to him, Putin linked the young innovator's work to Modi's programme: "Ultimately, your work helps you realise the call by Prime Minister Modi, 'Make in India', because it helps young people go out to find their own solutions and implement these solutions."

Who is Raul John Aju

Aju, widely called the 'AI Kid of India', is from Kerala and is a Class 12 commerce student at the Government Higher Secondary School in North Edappally, Kochi, according to The Times of India. He is the founder and chief technology officer of AI Realm Technologies and is associated with ThinkCraft Academy, which teaches students and professionals about AI. His creations include MeBot, RESQ AI, ZapGap, Investo AI and FeedFye, and an Onmanorama report in August 2026 counted around 15 AI tools built by him.

Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev also met young AI specialists at the conference, which runs from November 26 to 28 and brings together more than 300 Russian and international specialists to discuss AI in business, science and society.

A selfie, and a familiar theme

After the interaction, Aju shared a selfie and a video clip of his handshake with Putin on Instagram. "From making my first video in a bathroom at 9 to taking a selfie with President Putin, never in my wildest dreams did I think life would take me here," he wrote. "More than anything I've achieved, I'm grateful for the person this journey has helped me become."

It is not the first time Putin has praised the programme. In December 2024, at the VTB Russia Calling Investment Forum in Moscow, he highlighted 'Make in India' and described business conditions in India as favourable for investment. The initiative, launched in September 2014, aims to encourage domestic manufacturing, innovation, investment and employment.
